title: The book nobody can read
text: In a library at Yale University in the United States, there is a small book that has defeated some of the most brilliant minds of the last hundred years. It contains around two hundred and forty pages of elegant handwriting, accompanied by colourful drawings of plants, stars and strange human figures. The problem is that nobody knows what language it is written in, or whether it is a language at all.

The book is known as the Voynich manuscript, after Wilfrid Voynich, a Polish bookseller who bought it in 1912 from a religious college near Rome. Voynich was convinced that he had found something extraordinary and spent the rest of his life trying to understand it, without success. Since then, the manuscript has been studied by professional codebreakers, linguists, historians and thousands of enthusiastic amateurs. All of them have failed.

We do know a few things about it. In 2009, scientists used radiocarbon dating to analyse the animal skin on which the book is written, and concluded that it was made in the early fifteenth century, between about 1404 and 1438. This ruled out one popular theory, which claimed that the book was a fake created by Voynich himself. Letters found with the manuscript also show that it once belonged to an emperor in Prague, who is said to have paid a large amount of gold for it.

The contents, however, remain a complete mystery. About half of the book is filled with drawings of plants, but most of them do not match any species known to science. Other sections seem to show astronomical charts, while one particularly odd part contains images of small figures bathing in pools connected by pipes. The text itself uses an alphabet of around twenty to thirty symbols that appear nowhere else.

Over the years, people have suggested all kinds of explanations. Some believe it is written in a secret code designed to hide medical or scientific knowledge. Others think it may be an unknown language written in an invented alphabet. Statistical studies have shown that the text has some patterns typical of real languages, which makes it unlikely to be completely random. Yet every few years, someone announces that they have finally solved the puzzle, and every time their solution is quickly rejected by other experts.

Some researchers suspect that the most disappointing answer may also be the correct one: that the book is an elaborate hoax from the fifteenth century, written to impress or deceive a wealthy buyer. If so, its author would have needed great patience, since producing so many pages of convincing nonsense would have been extremely difficult.

Whatever its origin, the manuscript has become famous precisely because it refuses to give up its secret. Today, anyone can look at every page online, and new theories appear constantly. Perhaps one day someone will finally read it. Until then, it remains one of the most fascinating puzzles in the world.
